title: John Lear possibly fed disinformation to Lazar

tellings.quote: Bob Lazar would hang around some interesting characters. Guys like John Lear, who flew cargo planes for the CIA in the seventies.
His story was leaked to the public by a CIA pilot, a close friend of his named John Lear who flew cargo planes for the CIA and set all sorts of aviation records in the '70s.
tellings.difference: Says Lear leaked Lazar's story to the public, and adds his aviation records and the involvement of Knapp and Corbell.
tellings.link_reason: Both present John Lear, the CIA cargo pilot, as the man behind the Lazar story, possibly as a CIA operation.

as_told.title: John Lear outside Area 51 and the CIA pushing out the Lazar story

plain: A man named Bob Lazar, whose story about secret craft at Area 51, a hidden US test site in the Nevada desert, became famous, may have been fed false information by his close friend John Lear. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, across three episodes. He describes Lear as a pilot who flew cargo planes for the CIA, the US spy agency, in the 1970s and set many flying records. He says it was Lear who leaked Lazar's story to the public, together with the journalist George Knapp and the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell. In one episode Michels adds that Lear had spent a decade hanging around outside Area 51, where the guards knew him by sight. In that episode he goes further and says outright that the CIA pushed the Lazar story out. If true, this would mean Lazar's account was shaped by an intelligence agency. All three tellings come from Michels alone, and they differ only in how far he takes the idea.
